symbols.name: V
symbols.def: \(V\) indexes the observed variables.

symbols.name: Xv
symbols.def: \(X_v\in\{0,1\}\) is the observed variable at vertex \(v\in V\).

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: \(G=(V,E^{\to},E^{\leftrightarrow})\) is the latent projection of a recursive semi-Markovian causal model.

symbols.name: Edir
symbols.def: \(E^{\to}=\{(w,v):w\to v\text{ in }G\}\).

symbols.name: Ebi
symbols.def: \(E^{\leftrightarrow}=\{\{v,w\}:v\leftrightarrow w\text{ in }G\}\).

symbols.name: pa
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{pa}_G(v)=\{w\in V:(w,v)\in E^{\to}\}\).

symbols.name: districts
symbols.def: \(\mathcal D(G)\) is the partition of \(V\) into maximal bidirected-connected sets.

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: \(M\) assigns at most one sign to each directed edge whose parent effect is restricted.

symbols.name: Sv
symbols.def: \(S_v=\{w\in\operatorname{pa}_G(v):((w,v),s)\in M\text{ for some }s\in\{+1,-1\}\}\).

symbols.name: rv
symbols.def: \(r_v=|\operatorname{pa}_G(v)\setminus S_v|\).

symbols.name: Dm
symbols.def: \(D_m\) is the number of up-sets of the Boolean lattice \(\{0,1\}^m\), equivalently the number of isotone Boolean functions on \(m\) coordinates.

symbols.name: UG
symbols.def: \(U_G=\{u_v:v\in V\}\cup\{u_e:e\in E^{\leftrightarrow}\}\), with one private latent index per vertex and one shared latent index per bidirected edge.

symbols.name: chU
symbols.type: observed children of an exogenous index
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{ch}(u_v)=\{v\}\) and \(\operatorname{ch}(u_{\{v,w\}})=\{v,w\}\).

symbols.name: CU
symbols.def: \(C(u)\) is the maximal set of observed vertices reachable from \(\operatorname{ch}(u)\) through a chain of exogenous indices with successive indices sharing an observed child; in the latent projection it is the district containing \(\operatorname{ch}(u)\).

symbols.name: bU
symbols.def: \(b_u=\prod_{v\in C(u)}T_v\).

symbols.name: RGM
symbols.def: \(R_{G,M}=\prod_{u\in U_G}b_u\).

symbols.name: fv
symbols.def: \(f_v\) is the recursive response mechanism for \(X_v\).

symbols.name: OmegaU
symbols.def: \(\Omega_u\) is the support of the canonical exogenous variable indexed by \(u\in U_G\).

symbols.name: muU
symbols.def: \(\mu=\bigotimes_{u\in U_G}\mu_u\) is the product law of the semi-Markovian exogenous variables.

symbols.name: mfrak
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak m=(f,\mu)\) consists of binary structural mechanisms \(f_v\) and mutually independent exogenous laws indexed by \(U_G\).

symbols.name: Mclass
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak M(G,M)\) is the class in Definition \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: \(K\) is fixed and finite.

symbols.name: Zmenu
symbols.def: \(\mathcal Z=\{z_1,\ldots,z_K\}\) indexes full population laws, with the empty intervention allowed.

symbols.name: PZ
symbols.def: \(P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m)=(P_{\mathfrak m,z_k}(X_V=x):1\le k\le K,\ x\in\{0,1\}^{V})\).

symbols.name: AQ
symbols.space: finite conjunctions of binary potential-response literals
symbols.def: \(A_Q\) is a finite unnested event over potential responses generated by \(G\).

symbols.name: BQ
symbols.space: finite conjunctions of binary potential-response literals
symbols.def: \(B_Q\) is a finite unnested event over potential responses generated by \(G\).

symbols.name: Q
symbols.def: \(Q=(A_Q,B_Q)\) denotes the query \(P(A_Q\mid B_Q)\).

symbols.name: thetaQ
symbols.def: For every \(\mathfrak m\) with \(P_{\mathfrak m}(B_Q)>0\), \(\theta_Q(\mathfrak m)=P_{\mathfrak m}(A_Q\cap B_Q)/P_{\mathfrak m}(B_Q)\).

symbols.name: kappa
symbols.def: \(\kappa\) is a fixed positive constant.

symbols.name: Fiber
symbols.def: \(\mathcal F_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(p)=\{\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M(G,M):P_{\mathfrak m,z_k}(X_V)=p_k\text{ for every }k\}\).

symbols.name: IDcrit
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{GID}_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(Q)\) is the global menu-equivalence criterion in Definition \(\mathrm{def:identification\text{-}criterion}\).

symbols.name: OQ
symbols.def: \(\mathsf O_{G,M}(Q)\) is the construction in Definition \(\mathrm{def:order\text{-}amwn}\).

symbols.name: NQ
symbols.space: finite signed sums of district order cells
symbols.def: \(\mathsf N_{G,M}(Q)\) is the construction in Definition \(\mathrm{def:order\text{-}normal\text{-}form}\).

symbols.name: Rexpr
symbols.def: \(\mathcal R(p)\) is the grammar in Definition \(\mathrm{def:expression\text{-}grammar}\).

symbols.name: FAIL
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{FAIL}\) records that no identifying expression was returned by the procedure.

symbols.name: CTFID
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{CTFID}\) is the procedure of Correa, Lee, and Bareinboim.

symbols.name: MID
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{MID}\) is Algorithm 1 of Maiti, Plecko, and Bareinboim.

symbols.name: pstar
symbols.def: \(p^{\star}=P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m_0)=P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m_1)\) for a compiled nonidentification pair.

symbols.name: trace
symbols.def: \(\tau_{\mathsf F}(G,M,\mathcal Z,Q)\) records the two canonical structural profiles, exact algebraic product-simplex masses, sign conditions, positive denominators, common menu vector, and unequal query cross-product returned by the satisfiable nonidentification system.

symbols.name: nk
symbols.def: \(n_k\) is the independent sample size from regime \(z_k\).

symbols.name: rhok
symbols.def: \(\rho_k=\lim_{n\to\infty}n_k/n\).

symbols.name: phat
symbols.def: \(\widehat p=(\widehat p_1,\ldots,\widehat p_K)\), where \(\widehat p_k\) is the empirical multinomial cell vector in regime \(k\).

symbols.name: F
symbols.def: \(F\) is the finite expression returned by \(\mathsf{MCTFID}(G,M,\mathcal Z,Q)\).

symbols.name: lambdaF
symbols.def: \(\lambda_F(p)\) is the minimum absolute value, at \(p\), of every branch guard, every active-branch division denominator, every active isolated-root derivative, and every active root-to-isolating-interval endpoint distance in the finite expression tree \(F\); the minimum of an empty list is \(1\).

symbols.name: thetaHat
symbols.def: \(\widehat\theta_Q=F(\widehat p)\).

symbols.name: Sigmak
symbols.def: \(\Sigma_k=\operatorname{diag}(p_k)-p_kp_k^{\mathsf T}\).

symbols.name: sigma2
symbols.def: \(\sigma_F^2(p)=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\rho_k^{-1}\nabla_kF(p)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_k\nabla_kF(p)\).

symbols.name: sigmaHat
symbols.def: \(\widehat\sigma_F\) is obtained from \(\sigma_F(p)\) by substituting \(\widehat p_k\), \(n_k/n\), and the recursively evaluated gradients.

symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: \(\alpha\) indexes a two-sided Wald confidence interval.

symbols.name: CI
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{CI}_{1-\alpha}\) is the interval in Definition \(\mathrm{def:wald\text{-}interval}\).

symbols.name: Acan
symbols.def: \(A_{G,M}=\prod_{v\in V}T_v^{\prod_{u\in U_G:\,v\in\operatorname{ch}(u)}b_u}\).

assumptions.condition: \(V\) is finite and \(X_v\in\{0,1\}\) for every \(v\in V\).
\(G\) is acyclic and \(\mathfrak m\) has the recursive semi-Markovian expansion indexed by \(U_G\).

For every \(((w,v),s)\in M\), every latent assignment, and every fixed assignment of \(\operatorname{pa}_G(v)\setminus\{w\}\), the map \(x_w\mapsto f_v(x_{\operatorname{pa}_G(v)},u)\) is nondecreasing when \(s=+1\) and nonincreasing when \(s=-1\).
There exists one \(\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\) such that \(P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m)=p\).

standard.name: positive denominator for conditional counterfactual reduction

assumptions.condition: Within regime \(k\), the \(n_k\) observations are independent draws from \(p_k\), and samples from distinct regimes are independent.

standard.name: regular point of a finite piecewise-analytic functional, including a locally fixed branch

definitions.name: signed response types
definitions.construction: For each \(v\), sign-normalize a restricted parent by \(z_w=x_w\) for sign \(+1\) and \(z_w=1-x_w\) for sign \(-1\); a local type is a map assigning to every unrestricted-parent configuration an up-set of \(\{0,1\}^{m_v}\), so its count is \(T_v=D_{m_v}^{2^{r_v}}\).

definitions.name: canonical response bound
definitions.construction: Assign each \(u\in U_G\) at most \(b_u=\prod_{v\in C(u)}T_v\) support points; the induced joint latent assignment space has at most \(R_{G,M}=\prod_{u\in U_G}b_u\) points, and the vector of free exogenous masses has dimension at most \(\sum_{u\in U_G}(b_u-1)\).

definitions.name: Fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal F_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(p)=\{\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M(G,M):P_{\mathfrak m,z_k}(X_V=x)=p_k(x)\text{ for every }x\in\{0,1\}^{V}\text{ and }1\le k\le K\}\).

definitions.name: global signed-monotone functional-identification criterion
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{GID}_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(Q)=1\) exactly when, for every \(\mathfrak m_0,\mathfrak m_1\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\) with \(P_{\mathfrak m_i}(B_Q)>0\), \(P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m_0)=P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m_1)\) implies \(\theta_Q(\mathfrak m_0)=\theta_Q(\mathfrak m_1)\).

definitions.name: OQ
definitions.construction: Construct the ordinary ancestral multi-world network for the literals in \(A_Q\cup B_Q\); merge copies licensed by consistency and exclusion; sign-normalize every parent coordinate in \(S_v\); and annotate each pair of copies of \(X_v\) by the induced Boolean-lattice order relation between their normalized parent assignments. The resulting finite labeled mixed graph is \(\mathsf O_{G,M}(Q)\).

definitions.name: NQ
definitions.construction:
Apply the following construction separately to \(E=A_Q\cap B_Q\) and \(E=B_Q\). Let \(\mathcal T_v\) be the finite set of signed-isotone complete local response tables specified by Definition \(\mathrm{def:signed\text{-}response\text{-}types}\), and let \(R_v\) denote the realized complete local response table. For every \(t=(t_v)_{v\in V}\in\prod_{v\in V}\mathcal T_v\), recursively evaluate the literals of \(E\) in topological order in \(\mathsf O_{G,M}(Q)\), after deleting every local restriction inconsistent with the normalized Boolean-lattice order. If \(e_E(t)\in\{0,1\}\) is the resulting event indicator, define
\[
 \mathsf N_{G,M}(Q;E)
 =\sum_{t:e_E(t)=1}\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}
 \mathbf 1\{(R_v)_{v\in D}=t_D\},
\]
with terms ordered lexicographically by a fixed ordering of vertices and local tables. The two forms for \(A_Q\cap B_Q\) and \(B_Q\) constitute \(\mathsf N_{G,M}(Q)\). Thus the normal form is the expansion in the fixed exact response-type atom basis, rather than an unspecified choice among algebraically equivalent M\"obius expansions.

definitions.name: Rexpr
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal R(p)\) is the grammar of finite expression trees containing menu cells and rational constants and closed under finite sums, products, quotients on guarded positive denominators, and finite total branches guarded by rational polynomial sign conditions.  Its algebraic-section terms are \(\operatorname{Root}_j(h;I)\), when the active branch certifies that the rational interval \(I\) contains exactly the indexed real root of \(h(t,p)\), and \(\operatorname{ThomRoot}_{\sigma}(h)\), the unique real root whose derivative-sign vector has the finite Thom encoding \(\sigma\) on the active semialgebraic branch.  Every root term carries an existence-and-uniqueness guard, and every expression has a rational default on branches where that guard fails.  The polynomial \(h\) and all branch guards have rational coefficients.  At an arbitrary population vector \(p\), exact symbolic evaluation means evaluation in the ordered real field supplied with exact polynomial-sign queries: the active guard is selected by its exact sign vector and each root term denotes its uniquely certified real section.  When the coordinates of \(p\) are given exactly as rational or real-algebraic numbers, this semantics is implemented by a finite standard algorithm using algebraic arithmetic, sign determination, Thom encodings, and real-root isolation.  No finite bit-computation claim is made for an arbitrary transcendental input encoding without such a sign oracle.

definitions.name: MCTFID
definitions.construction:
Define \(\mathsf{MCTFID}(G,M,\mathcal Z,Q)\) by the following exact finite procedure.  First, if \(M=\varnothing\), run the published conditional \(\mathsf{CTFID}(G,\mathcal Z,Q)\); lift a successful expression unchanged into \(\mathcal R(p)\), and on failure continue directly to the certificate step below.  Second, if \(M\ne\varnothing\), run \(\mathsf{MID}(G,M,\mathcal Z,Q)\) and return its exact expression on success.  On failure of either applicable front end, enumerate the at most
\[
 A_{G,M}=\prod_{v\in V}T_v^{\prod_{u\in U_G:\,v\in\operatorname{ch}(u)}b_u}
\]
canonical signed-isotone structural-table profiles.  For each profile \(a\), use product-simplex mass coordinates \(\lambda\), the polynomial menu cells \(\phi_{a,k,x}(\lambda)\), and the polynomial counterfactual numerator and denominator \(h_a(\lambda)\) and \(d_a(\lambda)\).  Exact real quantifier elimination decides the finite disjunction over profile pairs imposing both product-simplex systems, \(d_{a_0}>0\), \(d_{a_1}>0\), equality of every \(\phi_{a_i,k,x}\), and
\[
 h_{a_0}d_{a_1}\ne h_{a_1}d_{a_0}.
\]
If the disjunction is satisfiable, exact algebraic sample-point extraction records the profiles, masses, sign conditions, common menu vector, and unequal cross-products in \(\tau_{\mathsf F}\), and the procedure returns \((\mathsf{FAIL},\tau_{\mathsf F})\).  If it is unsatisfiable, form the semialgebraic relation
\[
 \Gamma_Q=\{(p,t):\exists a,\lambda,\ \Lambda_a(\lambda),\ p=\phi_a(\lambda),\ d_a(\lambda)>0,\ t d_a(\lambda)=h_a(\lambda)\}.
\]
Use effective sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition and Thom encodings to compile its singleton fibers into a finite expression \(F\in\mathcal R(p)\), and set \(F(p)=0\) off the projection of \(\Gamma_Q\).  The procedure examines at most \(A_{G,M}\) profiles and \(A_{G,M}^2\) ordered profile pairs; a pair has at most \(2N_{G,M}=2\sum_{u\in U_G}(b_u-1)\) free mass coordinates, and each model sum has at most \(R_{G,M}\) joint latent monomials.

definitions.name: Cfail
definitions.construction: The failure compiler \(\mathsf C_{\mathsf F}\) is the exact decoder for the algebraic certificate \(\tau_{\mathsf F}\) returned by \(\mathsf{MCTFID}\).  It reads the two enumerated signed-isotone structural-table profiles and their exact algebraic product-simplex masses, deletes zero-mass padding states, and returns the resulting finite canonical models \((\mathfrak m_0,\mathfrak m_1)\) together with the recorded common menu vector \(p^{\star}\).  Before returning, it checks every simplex constraint, every structural-table sign constraint, every menu-cell equality, both strict denominator inequalities, and the unequal query cross-product.  Thus \(\mathsf C_{\mathsf F}\) decodes a globally checkable quantifier-elimination sample certificate; it is not a compiler from a district-local graphical failure trace.

definitions.name: lambdaF
definitions.construction: Traverse the finite expression tree \(F\) at \(p\), retain the guards and algebraic operations on the selected branch, and set \(\lambda_F(p)\) equal to the minimum of the absolute branch-guard values, active division denominators, active isolated-root derivatives, and active root-to-isolating-interval endpoint distances; set \(\lambda_F(p)=1\) if this list is empty.

definitions.name: thetaHat
definitions.construction: For a successful output \(F\in\mathcal R(p)\), evaluate the same finite expression tree at the empirical regime cell vectors: \(\widehat\theta_Q=F(\widehat p)\). On the locally selected branch certified by \(\lambda_F(p)>0\), differentiate sums, products, quotients, and isolated roots recursively to obtain \(\nabla_kF(\widehat p)\) whenever \(\widehat p\) remains on that branch.

definitions.name: plug-in Wald interval
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{CI}_{1-\alpha}=\bigl[\widehat\theta_Q-z_{1-\alpha/2}\widehat\sigma_F/\sqrt n,\widehat\theta_Q+z_{1-\alpha/2}\widehat\sigma_F/\sqrt n\bigr]\), where \(\widehat\sigma_F^2\) substitutes \(\widehat p_k\), \(n_k/n\), and \(\nabla_kF(\widehat p)\) into \(\sigma_F^2(p)\).

statements.statement: For every \(\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\), there exists a counterfactually equivalent finite \(\widetilde{\mathfrak m}\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\) whose local mechanism at \(v\) uses at most \(T_v=D_{m_v}^{2^{r_v}}\) signed-isotone response types and whose exogenous support satisfies \(|\Omega_u|\le b_u\) for every \(u\in U_G\). Hence every finite menu law and every finite counterfactual law are preserved using at most \(R_{G,M}\) joint latent configurations. If \(m_v>0\), then \(T_v<2^{2^{|\operatorname{pa}_G(v)|}}\), the unrestricted Boolean response-function count.
statements.justification: This theorem converts the shape restriction into an exact finite carrier and exposes the Dedekind-number reduction that all later certification uses.
statements.gap: ZhangTianBareinboim2022 proves finite canonical equivalence using all local response functions; it does not preserve and count a signed-isotone subfamily.
statements.consumer: DuarteEtAl2024 can delete every order-violating response type before constructing a bound program, and MaitiPleckoBareinboim2025 gains an exact finite oracle for implementation tests.
statements.proof_tex:
\paragraph{Response tables.}
Fix \(\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\).  For a complete exogenous assignment \(u\), define the local response table
\[
 R_v(u)(x_{\operatorname{pa}_G(v)})
 =f_v(x_{\operatorname{pa}_G(v)},u_{\operatorname{pa}_U(v)}).
\]
For \(w\in S_v\), put \(z_w=x_w\) when the sign of \(w\to v\) is \(+1\), and put \(z_w=1-x_w\) when it is \(-1\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:signed\text{-}local\text{-}monotonicity}\) implies, coordinate by coordinate, that the normalized table is nondecreasing in every \(z_w\).  Hence, for each fixed assignment of the \(r_v\) unrestricted parents, the normalized signed-parent assignments on which the output is one form an up-set of \(\{0,1\}^{m_v}\).  There are \(D_{m_v}\) such up-sets and \(2^{r_v}\) unrestricted-parent assignments.  Therefore the set \(\mathcal T_v\) of possible complete local response tables satisfies
\[
 |\mathcal T_v|\le D_{m_v}^{2^{r_v}}=T_v.
\]

\paragraph{A finite-dimensional barycenter lemma.}
We use the following elementary fact, proving it here to avoid any closed-convex-hull gap.  If a random vector \(Y\) takes values in a bounded set \(S\subset\mathbb R^q\), then \(E(Y)\in\operatorname{conv}(S)\).  Let \(C=\overline{\operatorname{conv}(S)}\), and induct on the affine dimension of \(C\).  Approximation of \(Y\) by simple random vectors gives \(E(Y)\in C\).  If \(E(Y)\in\operatorname{relint}(C)\), choose a sufficiently small relative simplex around \(E(Y)\) contained in \(C\).  Density of \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\) in \(C\) permits its vertices to be perturbed into \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\) while their convex hull still contains \(E(Y)\); convexity then gives \(E(Y)\in\operatorname{conv}(S)\).  Otherwise a supporting affine functional \(\ell\) at \(E(Y)\) satisfies \(\ell(y)\le \ell(E(Y))\) for every \(y\in C\).  The nonnegative random variable \(\ell(E(Y))-\ell(Y)\) has expectation zero, so it is zero almost surely.  Thus \(Y\) lies almost surely in the proper supporting face \(C\cap\{\ell=\ell(E(Y))\}\), and the induction hypothesis applies in its strictly smaller affine dimension.  The zero-dimensional case is immediate.  This proves membership in the actual convex hull, not merely in its closure.

If a convex representation in the affine hyperplane \(\sum_{j=1}^q y_j=1\) uses more than \(q\) points, affine dependence gives coefficients \(c_i\), not all zero, with \(\sum_i c_i=0\) and \(\sum_i c_i y_i=0\).  Moving the convex weights by \(-\varepsilon c_i\), with \(\varepsilon>0\) maximal subject to nonnegativity, deletes at least one point without changing the barycenter.  Iteration leaves at most \(q\) points.  Consequently, a simplex-valued random vector with \(q\) coordinates has a barycentric representation using at most \(q\) values from its actual range.

\paragraph{Finite support within districts.}
For a district \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), let
\[
 U_D=\{u\in U_G:C(u)=D\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal T_D=\prod_{v\in D}\mathcal T_v,
 \qquad
 q_D=|\mathcal T_D|le\prod_{v\in D}T_v.
\]
Every exogenous parent of a vertex in \(D\) belongs to \(U_D\), so the district response-table vector is a measurable map
\[
 R_D=(R_v:v\in D)=H_D(U_D)\in\mathcal T_D.
\]
The sets \(U_D\) are disjoint across districts, and their coordinates are independent by \(\mathrm{ass:semi\text{-}markovian}\).

Fix \(u_0\in U_D\), temporarily retaining the current laws of the other coordinates.  For a value \(a\) of \(u_0\), let
\[
 q_a(t)=P\{H_D(a,U_D\setminus\{u_0\})=t\},
 \qquad t\in\mathcal T_D.
\]
Each \(q_a\) lies in \(\Delta_{q_D-1}\), and the current law of \(R_D\) is the barycenter
\[
 \bar q=\int q_a\,d\mu_{u_0}(a).
\]
Apply the proved barycenter lemma to the actual range of \(a\mapsto q_a\), discarding at most a null set on which a chosen version is undefined.  The affine-dependence reduction then supplies values \(a_1,\ldots,a_\ell\) and weights \(\lambda_j\ge0\) such that
\[
 \ell\le q_D,
 \qquad
 \sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\lambda_j=1,
 \qquad
 \bar q=\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\lambda_jq_{a_j}.
\]
Replacing \(\mu_{u_0}\) by \(\sum_j\lambda_j\delta_{a_j}\) therefore leaves the complete law of \(R_D\) unchanged and preserves the product form of the exogenous law.  Perform this replacement successively for every \(u\in U_D\) and then for every district.  At each step the same argument is applied to the current laws, so the current district response-vector law is preserved.  Since \(U_G\) is finite, the construction terminates and gives
\[
 |\Omega_u|\le q_{C(u)}le\prod_{v\in C(u)}T_v=b_u
 \qquad (u\in U_G).
\]

The selected structural tables are unchanged and hence remain signed-isotone.  The construction preserves the response-table-vector law in each district.  Independence of the disjoint district exogenous blocks therefore preserves the joint law of the complete response-table vector.  By acyclicity, every finite vector of potential responses is a deterministic recursive function of that complete vector; its law is unchanged.  Thus the resulting \(\widetilde{\mathfrak m}\) belongs to \(\mathfrak M(G,M)\), is counterfactually equivalent to \(\mathfrak m\), and satisfies
\[
 \left|\prod_{u\in U_G}\Omega_u\right|
 \le\prod_{u\in U_G}b_u=R_{G,M}.
\]
In particular, every finite menu law and every finite counterfactual law are preserved.

Finally, \(S_v\) and \(\operatorname{pa}_G(v)\setminus S_v\) partition the parents, so \(|\operatorname{pa}_G(v)|=m_v+r_v\).  If \(m_v>0\), the Boolean map \(z\mapsto1-z_1\) is not isotone, whereas the unrestricted count includes every Boolean map.  Hence
\[
 D_{m_v}<2^{2^{m_v}},
 \qquad
 T_v=D_{m_v}^{2^{r_v}}
 <\left(2^{2^{m_v}}\right)^{2^{r_v}}
 =2^{2^{m_v+r_v}}
 =2^{2^{|\operatorname{pa}_G(v)|}}.
\]
This proves the strict response-type reduction and the theorem.

statements.statement: After finite enumeration of the signed-isotone structural tables, the global sentence \(\operatorname{GID}_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(Q)=1\) is decidable by exact real quantifier elimination. Each enumerated pair of canonical models uses at most \(2\sum_{u\in U_G}(b_u-1)\) free exogenous-mass variables and at most \(2R_{G,M}\) joint latent configurations in total. When the sentence is false, the same finite system returns \(\mathfrak m_0,\mathfrak m_1\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\) and their common law \(p^{\star}=P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m_0)=P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m_1)\), with positive query denominators and \(\theta_Q(\mathfrak m_0)\ne\theta_Q(\mathfrak m_1)\).
statements.justification: The finite decider prevents the proposal from confusing existence of a complete oracle with the harder graphical compression and certificate problem.
statements.gap: ZhangTianBareinboim2022 and DuarteEtAl2024 optimize finite response-type programs, while neither states the signed arbitrary-menu conditional identification decision and explicit two-model extraction theorem.
statements.consumer: The decider supplies a regression oracle that can falsify candidate rules in Maiti's M-ID implementation and generate minimal failing examples for the graphical calculus.
statements.proof_tex:
By Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:signed\text{-}canonical\text{-}reduction}\), it suffices to quantify over canonical models satisfying Definition \(\mathrm{def:canonical\text{-}bound}\).  Pad every support of size smaller than \(b_u\) by zero-mass states.  For a fixed finite enumeration \(a\) of the signed-isotone structural tables, write
\[
 \lambda_{u,j}\ge0,
 \qquad
 \sum_{j=1}^{b_u}\lambda_{u,j}=1.
\]
Eliminating \(\lambda_{u,b_u}\) leaves at most \(\sum_{u\in U_G}(b_u-1)\) free real mass coordinates for one model.

For \(\omega\in\prod_u\{1,\ldots,b_u\}\), its product-law probability is the monomial
\[
 w_\lambda(\omega)=\prod_{u\in U_G}\lambda_{u,\omega_u}.
\]
The profile \(a\) and regime \(z_k\) deterministically produce an outcome \(X^{a,z_k}(\omega)\).  Hence every menu cell is the integer-coefficient polynomial
\[
 \phi_{a,k,x}(\lambda)
 =\sum_{\omega}
 \mathbf 1\{X^{a,z_k}(\omega)=x\}w_\lambda(\omega).
\]
Recursive evaluation of the counterfactual literals likewise gives the denominator and numerator polynomials
\[
 d_a(\lambda)=\sum_{\omega}\mathbf 1\{B_Q(\omega)\}w_\lambda(\omega),
 \qquad
 h_a(\lambda)=\sum_{\omega}\mathbf 1\{A_Q(\omega)\cap B_Q(\omega)\}w_\lambda(\omega).
\]
Every displayed sum has at most \(R_{G,M}\) monomials.

Let \(\Lambda_a(\lambda)\) denote the simplex equalities and inequalities for profile \(a\).  Nonidentification is exactly the finite disjunction, over ordered profile pairs \((a_0,a_1)\), of
\[
 \exists\lambda^0,\lambda^1\;\left[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\Lambda_{a_0}(\lambda^0)\wedge\Lambda_{a_1}(\lambda^1),\\
 &d_{a_0}(\lambda^0)>0\wedge d_{a_1}(\lambda^1)>0,\\
 &\phi_{a_0,k,x}(\lambda^0)=\phi_{a_1,k,x}(\lambda^1)
       &&\text{for every \(k,x\)},\\
 &h_{a_0}(\lambda^0)d_{a_1}(\lambda^1)
   \ne h_{a_1}(\lambda^1)d_{a_0}(\lambda^0).
 \end{aligned}\right]
\]
The last line is equivalent to inequality of the conditional query values because both denominators are positive.  Each disjunct has at most \(2\sum_{u\in U_G}(b_u-1)\) free mass coordinates.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}real\text{-}closed\text{-}field\text{-}decision}\) decides this rational semialgebraic sentence and extracts an exact algebraic sample point whenever it is satisfiable.

If a disjunct is satisfiable, its profiles and sampled mass vectors define \(\mathfrak m_0,\mathfrak m_1\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\).  Their tables are signed-isotone, their exogenous laws have the required product form, and the sampled strict inequalities give positive query denominators.  For every menu cell,
\[
 p^\star_{k,x}
 =\phi_{a_0,k,x}(\lambda^0)
 =\phi_{a_1,k,x}(\lambda^1),
\]
while the cross-product inequality gives \(\theta_Q(\mathfrak m_0)\ne\theta_Q(\mathfrak m_1)\).  Each model uses at most \(R_{G,M}\) joint latent configurations, so the pair uses at most \(2R_{G,M}\).

Conversely, if \(\operatorname{GID}_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(Q)=0\), Definition \(\mathrm{def:identification\text{-}criterion}\) gives two models with a common menu law, positive denominators, and unequal query values.  Apply Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:signed\text{-}canonical\text{-}reduction}\) to each.  Counterfactual equivalence preserves every menu cell, the numerator, and the denominator, so the resulting canonical pair satisfies one displayed disjunct.  Thus the disjunction is satisfiable exactly when the global identification criterion is false.  Effective real quantifier elimination decides the criterion, and exact sample-point extraction proves the asserted countermodel conclusion.

statements.statement: For every finite unnested event \(A_Q\cap B_Q\), \(\mathsf N_{G,M}(Q)\) is a unique finite signed sum of order-consistent cells. Each summand factors into one response-type cell per district in \(\mathcal D(G)\), every deleted cell has probability zero in every \(\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\), and summing the normal form equals \(P_{\mathfrak m}(A_Q\cap B_Q)\) for every such model. The same claim holds for \(B_Q\).
statements.justification: A canonical order normal form is the bridge between local monotonicity identities and district-level identification requests.
statements.gap: CorreaBareinboim2025 makes counterfactual independences explicit in an AMWN, and MaitiPleckoBareinboim2025 reduces selected ordered pairs, but neither supplies a unique signed order-cell normal form with district factorization.
statements.consumer: The AMWN and ctf-calculus toolchain can use this normal form as a deterministic intermediate representation for symbolic identification and audit trails.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathcal T_v\) be the finite signed-isotone response-table set and put \(\mathcal T=\prod_{v\in V}\mathcal T_v\).  A complete table vector \(t\in\mathcal T\), together with the acyclic directed order of \(G\), determines every potential-response literal in an unnested event by recursive substitution.  Thus, for \(E=A_Q\cap B_Q\), there is a well-defined indicator \(e_E(t)\in\{0,1\}\).

For a district \(D\), set
\[
 C_D(t_D)=\{(R_v:v\in D)=t_D\},
 \qquad
 C(t)=\bigcap_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}C_D(t_D).
\]
The exact response-table atoms are pairwise disjoint and partition the formal complete response-table space.  Consequently,
\[
 \mathbf 1_E
 =\sum_{t\in\mathcal T:e_E(t)=1}\mathbf 1_{C(t)}
 =\sum_{t\in\mathcal T:e_E(t)=1}
   \prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\mathbf 1_{C_D(t_D)}.
\]
This is a finite signed sum, with every nonzero coefficient equal to \(+1\), and each summand has exactly one response-type cell per district.

The expansion is unique in the fixed exact-atom basis of Definition \(\mathrm{def:order\text{-}normal\text{-}form}\).  Indeed, if \(\mathbf 1_E=\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}c_t\mathbf 1_{C(t)}\) as a formal atom expansion, evaluation at the atom indexed by \(t_0\) gives \(c_{t_0}=e_E(t_0)\).  The stipulated lexicographic ordering changes only the order of display.

For every signed parent coordinate, Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:signed\text{-}local\text{-}monotonicity}\) makes the normalized response table isotone.  A cell demanding output one at \(z\) and output zero at a comparable \(z'\ge z\) is therefore empty.  These are exactly the local restrictions deleted by the order normalizer, so every deleted cell has probability zero under every \(\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\).

Every exogenous index affecting a vertex in a district \(D\) has \(C(u)=D\).  Hence distinct district response vectors depend on disjoint exogenous-coordinate blocks.  The product exogenous law in \(\mathrm{ass:semi\text{-}markovian}\) gives
\[
 P_{\mathfrak m}\{C(t)\}
 =\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}P_{\mathfrak m}\{C_D(t_D)\}.
\]
Taking expectations in the atom identity yields
\[
 P_{\mathfrak m}(A_Q\cap B_Q)
 =\sum_{t:e_E(t)=1}
   \prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}P_{\mathfrak m}\{C_D(t_D)\},
\]
which is the value of \(\mathsf N_{G,M}(Q;A_Q\cap B_Q)\).  Repeating the same argument with \(E=B_Q\) proves the second assertion.

statements.statement: When \(M=\varnothing\), for every \(v\in V\) one has \(m_v=0\), \(r_v=|\operatorname{pa}_G(v)|\), \(D_0=2\), and therefore \(T_v=D_0^{2^{r_v}}=2^{2^{|\operatorname{pa}_G(v)|}}\), exactly the unrestricted Boolean response-function count. All order annotations are then vacuous, \(\mathsf N_{G,\varnothing}(Q)\) is the ordinary AMWN event normalization, and the completed \(\mathsf{MCTFID}(G,\varnothing,\mathcal Z,Q)\) has the same success set and returns an algebraically equivalent functional as \(\mathsf{CTFID}(G,\mathcal Z,Q)\).
statements.justification: The theorem gives a noncircular regression test: both the response atoms and the first algorithm branch collapse exactly to the published unrestricted procedure.
statements.gap: CorreaLeeBareinboim2021 supplies unrestricted conditional completeness; the new step is the exact empty-sign collapse of the signed type system and dispatch rule.
statements.consumer: Implementers can use ordinary CTFID outputs as exact regression tests for every empty-sign execution.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Assume \(M=\varnothing\), and fix \(v\in V\). By the definition of the signed-parent set,
\[
 S_v=\varnothing,
 \qquad
 m_v=|S_v|=0,
 \qquad
 r_v=|\operatorname{pa}_G(v)\setminus S_v|
     =|\operatorname{pa}_G(v)|.
\]
The Boolean lattice \(\{0,1\}^{0}\) has one element. Its only up-sets are the empty set and the whole singleton, so \(D_0=2\). More explicitly, for each of the \(2^{r_v}\) unrestricted-parent configurations, Definition \(\mathrm{def:signed\text{-}response\text{-}types}\) chooses one of those two up-sets. Membership of the unique lattice element in the chosen up-set is an arbitrary output bit. Consequently this choice is in bijection with an arbitrary Boolean map
\[
 \{0,1\}^{\operatorname{pa}_G(v)}\longrightarrow\{0,1\}.
\]
Thus the local atoms are exactly the unrestricted Boolean response functions, and not merely an equinumerous collection. Their number is
\[
 T_v=D_{m_v}^{2^{r_v}}
     =D_0^{2^{r_v}}
     =2^{2^{|\operatorname{pa}_G(v)|}}.
\]

There is no signed coordinate to normalize or compare. Therefore the extra order labels in Definition \(\mathrm{def:order\text{-}amwn}\) impose no restriction beyond the ordinary ancestral multi-world network. Since the local response-table atoms just exhibited are precisely the unrestricted atoms, the fixed exact-atom expansion of Definition \(\mathrm{def:order\text{-}normal\text{-}form}\) is precisely the ordinary AMWN event normalization. This proves the asserted collapse of \(\mathsf N_{G,\varnothing}(Q)\).

It remains to prove equality of the two success sets, including the failure branch. First suppose that \(\mathsf{CTFID}(G,\mathcal Z,Q)\) succeeds with expression \(H\). The first branch of Definition \(\mathrm{def:mctfid\text{-}handle}\) runs that procedure when \(M=\varnothing\) and returns \(H\) immediately, merely viewing it as an element of \(\mathcal R(p)\). Hence the two returned functionals are algebraically equivalent; indeed, the expression is unchanged.

Conversely, suppose that \(\mathsf{CTFID}(G,\mathcal Z,Q)\) fails. When \(M=\varnothing\), signed local monotonicity is vacuous, so Definition \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\) gives exactly the finite-binary unrestricted recursive semi-Markovian class. By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}ctfid\text{-}completeness}\), failure of \(\mathsf{CTFID}\) means that the positive-denominator conditional query is not identifiable on this class. Definition \(\mathrm{def:identification\text{-}criterion}\) therefore gives
\[
 \operatorname{GID}_{G,\varnothing,\mathcal Z}(Q)=0.
\]
Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}decision}\) now says that the finite pair system examined by the continuation is satisfiable: it has two legal models \(\mathfrak m_0,\mathfrak m_1\in\mathfrak M(G,\varnothing)\) with positive query denominators and
\[
 P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m_0)=P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m_1),
 \qquad
 \theta_Q(\mathfrak m_0)\ne\theta_Q(\mathfrak m_1).
\]
By the terminal branches of Definition \(\mathrm{def:mctfid\text{-}handle}\), exact quantifier elimination detects this satisfiable system, extracts its sample certificate, and returns \((\mathsf{FAIL},\tau_{\mathsf F})\). Thus \(\mathsf{MCTFID}\) cannot succeed after an empty-sign \(\mathsf{CTFID}\) failure. Combining the two cases proves equality of success sets and algebraic equivalence of the successful outputs. Notice that the \(M\ne\varnothing\) \(\mathsf{MID}\) branch is never invoked in this argument. \(\square\)

statements.statement: If \(\mathsf{MCTFID}(G,M,\mathcal Z,Q)=F\in\mathcal R(p)\), then under \(\mathrm{ass:menu\text{-}compatibility}\), \(\mathrm{ass:positive\text{-}query\text{-}denominator}\), \(\mathrm{ass:independent\text{-}regime\text{-}sampling}\), \(\mathrm{ass:stable\text{-}regime\text{-}shares}\), \(\mathrm{ass:analytic\text{-}branch\text{-}margin}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:nondegenerate\text{-}variance}\), the empirical vector remains on the branch selected at \(p\) with probability tending to one and \(\sqrt n\{F(\widehat p)-F(p)\}\rightsquigarrow N(0,\sigma_F^2(p))\). For every generating \(\mathfrak m\in\mathcal F_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(p)\), the branch-local recursively differentiated variance estimator is consistent and \(P_{\mathfrak m}\{\theta_Q(\mathfrak m)\in\mathsf{CI}_{1-\alpha}\}\to1-\alpha\).
statements.justification: A complete identification calculus needs a generic route from finite menu cells to uncertainty quantification under the same denominator conditions used by the query.
statements.gap: BhattacharyaNabiShpitser2022 compiles ordinary hidden-variable effect formulas into estimators, while MaitiPleckoBareinboim2025 reports bootstrap intervals without a limit theorem for arbitrary successful signed counterfactual formulas.
statements.consumer: Analysts using the Causal Fairness Analysis toolkit can attach reproducible standard errors and Wald intervals to any fixed successful finite-cell output.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Put \(d=2^{|V|}\), fix an enumeration \(x_1,\ldots,x_d\) of \(\{0,1\}^{V}\), and fix an arbitrary generating model
\[
 \mathfrak m\in\mathcal F_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(p).
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:menu\text{-}compatibility}\) ensures that this fiber is nonempty.  By Definition \(\mathrm{def:menu\text{-}fiber}\), membership of \(\mathfrak m\) gives
\[
 P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m)=p. \tag{1}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:positive\text{-}query\text{-}denominator}\) gives
\[
 P_{\mathfrak m}(B_Q)\geq\kappa>0. \tag{2}
\]
The successful-output soundness clause of Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}oracle\text{-}complete\text{-}mctfid}\), applied to
\[
 \mathsf{MCTFID}(G,M,\mathcal Z,Q)=F\in\mathcal R(p),
\]
therefore yields
\[
 F\bigl(P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m)\bigr)=\theta_Q(\mathfrak m). \tag{3}
\]
Combining (1) and (3) proves the causal centering identity
\[
 F(p)=\theta_Q(\mathfrak m). \tag{4}
\]
Thus the causal target is not identified with the observed-law functional by definition; equality (4) follows from successful-output soundness and the positive-denominator condition.

We next establish local regularity.  The expression tree of \(F\) is finite, and Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:analytic\text{-}branch\text{-}margin}\) states that
\[
 \lambda_F(p)\geq\kappa>0. \tag{5}
\]
We claim that there are an ambient open neighborhood \(U\subset\mathbb R^{Kd}\) of \(p\) and a continuously differentiable map \(F_p^{\circ}:U\to\mathbb R\) such that \(F(q)=F_p^{\circ}(q)\) for every \(q\in U\) in the domain of the expression grammar.  On \(U\), the finite branch selected at \(p\) is unchanged, every active quotient denominator remains nonzero, and every active root selector returns the continuation of the root selected at \(p\).

We prove the claim by induction through the finite active expression tree.  Cell coordinates and rational constants are analytic, and finite sums and products preserve continuous differentiability.  If \(a(q)/b(q)\) is an active quotient, Definition \(\mathrm{def:analytic\text{-}branch\text{-}margin}\) and (5) give \(|b(p)|\geq\kappa\).  Continuity gives a neighborhood on which \(|b(q)|\geq\kappa/2\).  If a total finite branch is selected by polynomial sign guards \(g_1,\ldots,g_s\), then (5) gives \(|g_j(p)|\geq\kappa\) for every active guard.  After shrinking the neighborhood, every \(g_j(q)\) has the same sign as \(g_j(p)\), so the branch is fixed.

Consider an active rational-interval root node.  Write
\[
 t_0=\operatorname{Root}_j(h;I)(p),
 \qquad h(t_0,p)=0,
 \qquad I=(a,b).
\]
The margin in (5) implies
\[
 |\partial_t h(t_0,p)|\geq\kappa,
 \qquad
 \min\{t_0-a,b-t_0\}\geq\kappa. \tag{6}
\]
Choose \(0<\varepsilon<\kappa/2\).  Because \(h\) is a polynomial and \(\partial_t h(t_0,p)\neq0\), there is a neighborhood \(U_0\) of \(p\) on which \(\partial_t h(t,q)\) has constant sign and absolute value at least \(\kappa/2\) whenever \(|t-t_0|\leq\varepsilon\).  At \(q=p\), the mean-value theorem makes \(h(t_0-\varepsilon,p)\) and \(h(t_0+\varepsilon,p)\) have opposite signs.  After shrinking \(U_0\), the same holds for every \(q\in U_0\).  The intermediate-value theorem and strict monotonicity in \(t\) consequently give a unique root
\[
 t(q)\in(t_0-\varepsilon,t_0+\varepsilon). \tag{7}
\]
Because \(I\) isolates \(t_0\) at \(p\), the continuous function \(|h(\,\cdot\,,p)|\) has a positive minimum on the compact set
\[
 [a,b]\setminus(t_0-\varepsilon,t_0+\varepsilon).
\]
Continuity of the polynomial coefficients permits a further shrinking of \(U_0\) on which no root enters that compact set or crosses an endpoint of \(I\).  The active existence, uniqueness, and index guards retain their signs.  Hence the exact \(\operatorname{Root}_j(h;I)\) selector equals \(t(q)\) throughout this smaller neighborhood.

For an active Thom selector
\[
 t_0=\operatorname{ThomRoot}_{\sigma}(h)(p),
\]
the active guard certifies that \(t_0\) is the unique real root with the displayed Thom encoding.  The isolated-root derivative is part of the margin, so
\[
 h(t_0,p)=0,
 \qquad |\partial_t h(t_0,p)|\geq\kappa. \tag{8}
\]
The same local monotonicity argument gives a unique continuous root continuation \(t(q)\) near \(t_0\).  The finitely many polynomial sign predicates in the selected Thom branch are active guards; by (5) their defining nonzero values retain their signs after another shrinking.  The active uniqueness guard therefore shows that \(\operatorname{ThomRoot}_{\sigma}(h)(q)=t(q)\).

For either root syntax, take \(q,q'\) in a sufficiently small common neighborhood.  The mean-value theorem in \(t\), the lower bound on \(|\partial_t h|\), and local Lipschitz continuity of the polynomial in its parameter coordinates give a finite constant \(C\) such that
\[
 |t(q)-t(q')|
 \leq \frac{2}{\kappa}
       |h(t(q'),q)-h(t(q'),q')|
 \leq C\|q-q'\|. \tag{9}
\]
Apply a coordinatewise difference quotient to \(h(t(q),q)=0\), use (9), and pass to the limit.  This gives
\[
 \nabla t(q)
 =-\frac{\nabla_q h(t(q),q)}{\partial_t h(t(q),q)}. \tag{10}
\]
The right-hand side is continuous after one more shrinking.  Formula (10) is exactly the recursive differentiation rule for either root syntax.  Intersecting the finitely many neighborhoods for all active guards, quotients, and roots proves the claim.  In particular,
\[
 q\longmapsto\nabla F_p^{\circ}(q)
 \quad\text{is continuous on }U. \tag{11}
\]
This is an ambient extension, so (11) remains valid even when some cells of \(p\) lie on the boundary of their probability simplices.  No positivity or rank condition on individual multinomial cells is needed.

We now derive the joint sampling limit.  For observation \(i\) in regime \(k\), define the one-hot vector
\[
 Y_{ki}=\bigl(\mathbf 1\{X_{ki}=x_1\},\ldots,
                    \mathbf 1\{X_{ki}=x_d\}\bigr)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
By Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:independent\text{-}regime\text{-}sampling}\), these vectors are independent and identically distributed within each regime, samples from distinct regimes are independent, and
\[
 E(Y_{ki})=p_k,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}(Y_{ki})
 =\operatorname{diag}(p_k)-p_kp_k^{\mathsf T}
 =\Sigma_k. \tag{12}
\]
Their coordinates are bounded, so all second moments exist.  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:stable\text{-}regime\text{-}shares}\) implies \(n_k\to\infty\) and
\[
 \frac{n}{n_k}\longrightarrow\rho_k^{-1}. \tag{13}
\]
Apply Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:multivariate\text{-}iid\text{-}clt}\) in each regime.  Independence across the fixed finite number \(K\) of regimes makes the joint characteristic function the product of the regime characteristic functions.  Together with (13), this yields
\[
 \sqrt n\,(\widehat p-p)
 \rightsquigarrow
 N_{Kd}(0,\Omega),
 \qquad
 \Omega=\operatorname{blockdiag}
 \bigl(\rho_1^{-1}\Sigma_1,\ldots,
       \rho_K^{-1}\Sigma_K\bigr). \tag{14}
\]
The covariance in (14) may be singular because every multinomial cell vector sums to one; the multivariate central limit theorem permits a singular covariance, so no rank assumption is required.  Directly from (12),
\[
 E_{\mathfrak m}\|\widehat p-p\|^2
 =\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_k)}{n_k}
 \longrightarrow0. \tag{15}
\]
Markov's inequality gives \(\widehat p\to p\) in probability.  Since \(U\) is a neighborhood of \(p\),
\[
 P_{\mathfrak m}(\widehat p\in U)\longrightarrow1. \tag{16}
\]
This is the asserted branch-stability conclusion.

On the event in (16), \(F(\widehat p)=F_p^{\circ}(\widehat p)\).  Apply Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}dimensional\text{-}delta\text{-}method}\) to (14) and the ambient derivative in (11).  Equality with probability tending to one transfers its conclusion from \(F_p^{\circ}\) to \(F\).  The scalar variance is
\[
 \nabla F(p)^{\mathsf T}\Omega\nabla F(p)
 =\sum_{k=1}^{K}\rho_k^{-1}
   \nabla_kF(p)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_k\nabla_kF(p)
 =\sigma_F^2(p). \tag{17}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \sqrt n\{F(\widehat p)-F(p)\}
 \rightsquigarrow N\bigl(0,\sigma_F^2(p)\bigr). \tag{18}
\]

For variance consistency, put
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_k
 =\operatorname{diag}(\widehat p_k)
  -\widehat p_k\widehat p_k^{\mathsf T}.
\]
On the event in (16), equations (11), (13), and (15) imply, for every \(k\),
\[
 \nabla_kF(\widehat p)\to\nabla_kF(p),
 \qquad
 \widehat\Sigma_k\to\Sigma_k,
 \qquad
 (n_k/n)^{-1}\to\rho_k^{-1} \tag{19}
\]
in probability.  The branch-local standard-error rule may be assigned any fixed finite completion when its local recursive evaluation is unavailable; this choice is immaterial because the complement of (16) has probability tending to zero.  Substitution into the finite sum therefore gives
\[
 \widehat\sigma_F^2
 =\sum_{k=1}^{K}(n_k/n)^{-1}
   \nabla_kF(\widehat p)^{\mathsf T}
   \widehat\Sigma_k
   \nabla_kF(\widehat p)
 \longrightarrow\sigma_F^2(p) \tag{20}
\]
in probability.  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:nondegenerate\text{-}variance}\) states that \(\sigma_F^2(p)>0\).  Hence
\[
 \widehat\sigma_F\longrightarrow\sigma_F(p)>0 \tag{21}
\]
in probability.

Combining (18), (21), and Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:slutsky\text{-}studentization}\) gives
\[
 \frac{\sqrt n\{F(\widehat p)-F(p)\}}
      {\widehat\sigma_F}
 \rightsquigarrow N(0,1), \tag{22}
\]
where the ratio may be assigned any fixed value on \(\{\widehat\sigma_F=0\}\), an event whose probability tends to zero by (21).  On the event \(\{\widehat p\in U,\widehat\sigma_F>0\}\), whose probability tends to one, (4) and Definition \(\mathrm{def:wald\text{-}interval}\) give
\[
 \left\{
 \theta_Q(\mathfrak m)\in\mathsf{CI}_{1-\alpha}
 \right\}
 =
 \left\{
 \left|
 \frac{\sqrt n\{F(\widehat p)-F(p)\}}
      {\widehat\sigma_F}
 \right|
 \leq z_{1-\alpha/2}
 \right\}. \tag{23}
\]
The standard normal distribution has no mass at either boundary point in (23).  Weak convergence in (22), together with the vanishing probability of the complementary event, therefore implies
\[
 P_{\mathfrak m}\!\left\{
 \theta_Q(\mathfrak m)\in\mathsf{CI}_{1-\alpha}
 \right\}
 \longrightarrow
 P\{|Z|\leq z_{1-\alpha/2}\}
 =1-\alpha,
 \qquad Z\sim N(0,1). \tag{24}
\]
The model \(\mathfrak m\) was arbitrary in the fiber, and every such model induces the same regime-law vector \(p\).  Hence the argument applies to every generating \(\mathfrak m\in\mathcal F_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(p)\).  This proves every assertion. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Fix the class in which \(V\) is finite, every \(X_v\) is binary, \(G\) is acyclic, every model has the recursive semi-Markovian expansion indexed by \(U_G\), and every edge in \(M\) obeys its stated signed local-monotonicity restriction; equivalently, fix this paper's class \(\mathfrak M(G,M)\) of Definition \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\).  On this finite-binary recursive semi-Markovian signed-local-monotonicity class there is an effective finite procedure \(\mathsf{MCTFID}\), with failure decoder \(\mathsf C_{\mathsf F}\), having the following properties for every \((G,M,\mathcal Z,Q)\).  Put
\[
 N_{G,M}=\sum_{u\in U_G}(b_u-1),
 \qquad
 A_{G,M}=\prod_{v\in V}T_v^{\prod_{u\in U_G:\,v\in\operatorname{ch}(u)}b_u}.
\]
The procedure enumerates at most \(A_{G,M}\) canonical signed-isotone structural profiles, tests at most \(A_{G,M}^2\) ordered profile pairs, uses at most \(2N_{G,M}\) free mass coordinates and \(2R_{G,M}\) joint latent configurations per pair, and makes finitely many exact quantifier-elimination, sample-point, and cylindrical-decomposition calls on the resulting rational polynomial systems.  It returns a globally totalized \(F\in\mathcal R(p)\) if and only if \(\operatorname{GID}_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(Q)=1\), and then
\[
 F(P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m))=\theta_Q(\mathfrak m)
\]
for every \(\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\) with \(P_{\mathfrak m}(B_Q)>0\).  Otherwise it returns \((\mathsf{FAIL},\tau_{\mathsf F})\), and \(\mathsf C_{\mathsf F}(G,M,\mathcal Z,Q,\tau_{\mathsf F})=(\mathfrak m_0,\mathfrak m_1,p^{\star})\) gives two finite district-factorized signed-isotone SCMs satisfying \(|\Omega_u|\le b_u\), positive query denominators,
\[
 P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m_0)=p^{\star}=P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m_1),
 \qquad
 \theta_Q(\mathfrak m_0)\ne\theta_Q(\mathfrak m_1).
\]
When \(M=\varnothing\), the success branch is definitionally the unchanged lift of \(\mathsf{CTFID}\) and has exactly the \(\mathsf{CTFID}\) success set on this domain.  When \(M\ne\varnothing\), every successful \(\mathsf{MID}\) output on this domain is returned unchanged.  If \(M=\varnothing\) and \(\mathsf{MID}\) succeeds on this domain, only success-set containment is asserted: soundness of \(\mathsf{MID}\) and completeness of conditional \(\mathsf{CTFID}\) imply that \(\mathsf{MCTFID}\) succeeds, but its expression need not be the literal \(\mathsf{MID}\) expression.  Consequently, when all success sets below are restricted to this same finite-binary recursive semi-Markovian domain,
\[
 \operatorname{Succ}(\mathsf{MID})
 \subseteq\operatorname{Succ}(\mathsf{MCTFID})
 =\{(G,M,\mathcal Z,Q):\operatorname{GID}_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(Q)=1\}.
\]
This is scoped oracle completeness on this paper's class; it does not assert completeness on the broader ordered-variable or general-SCM domain considered by the published \(\mathsf{MID}\) work.  No claim is made here that the first inclusion is strict or that the finite oracle has a district-compositional graphical failure trace.
statements.justification: This is the scoped headline: on the finite-binary recursive semi-Markovian signed-local-monotonicity class, it gives an evaluable identifying expression for every identified instance and an exact finite countermodel certificate otherwise.
statements.gap: MaitiPleckoBareinboim2025 leaves a sufficient-and-necessary algorithm open on its broader ordered-variable/general-SCM domain; this theorem proves oracle completeness on the finite-binary recursive semi-Markovian subclass by signed-isotone canonical enumeration and exact real algebraic decision, without claiming a graphical converse compiler or resolution of that broader open problem.
statements.consumer: On the common finite-binary recursive semi-Markovian domain, Maiti's M-ID implementation can use the procedure as an exact regression oracle, while the PleckoBareinboim2024 fairness toolkit receives either an identifying functional or a checkable two-model obstruction.
statements.proof_tex:
\paragraph{Scope and finite parameterization.}
Throughout the proof, the input belongs to the class stated in the theorem: \(V\) is finite, all endogenous variables are binary, \(G\) is acyclic, the exogenous law has the recursive semi-Markovian product expansion indexed by \(U_G\), and the local tables obey the signs in \(M\).  These are exactly Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}binary}\), \(\mathrm{ass:semi\text{-}markovian}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:signed\text{-}local\text{-}monotonicity}\), hence exactly the models in Definition \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\).  No model outside this domain is quantified over below.

For \(v\in V\), write
\[
 U(v)=\{u\in U_G:v\in\operatorname{ch}(u)\}.
\]
By Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:signed\text{-}canonical\text{-}reduction}\), every model relevant to menu equivalence may be replaced, without changing any finite menu or counterfactual law, by one satisfying \(|\Omega_u|\le b_u\) for every \(u\).  Pad a smaller support with zero-mass states so that its displayed support has exactly \(b_u\) states.  For a fixed configuration of the exogenous parents indexed by \(U(v)\), the mechanism at \(v\) selects one of at most \(T_v\) signed-isotone complete response tables.  There are \(\prod_{u\in U(v)}b_u\) such exogenous configurations.  Consequently, the number of joint structural-table profiles is at most
\[
 \prod_{v\in V}T_v^{\prod_{u\in U(v)}b_u}
 =\prod_{v\in V}T_v^{\prod_{u\in U_G:\,v\in\operatorname{ch}(u)}b_u}
 =A_{G,M}.
\]
Here and below an empty product equals one.  All support bounds are positive integers because every \(T_v\) counts a nonempty finite response-table set.

Fix one enumerated profile \(a\).  Its remaining parameters are the product-simplex masses
\[
 \lambda_{u,j}\ge 0,
 \qquad
 \sum_{j=1}^{b_u}\lambda_{u,j}=1.
\]
Eliminating one mass from each simplex leaves at most
\[
 N_{G,M}=\sum_{u\in U_G}(b_u-1)
\]
free coordinates for one model and at most \(2N_{G,M}\) for an ordered pair.  A model sum ranges over at most
\[
 \prod_{u\in U_G}b_u=R_{G,M}
\]
joint latent configurations, and hence a pair uses at most \(2R_{G,M}\) such configurations.

For this profile, let \(\phi_{a,k,x}(\lambda)\), \(h_a(\lambda)\), and \(d_a(\lambda)\) be the menu-cell, query-numerator, and query-denominator polynomials constructed in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}decision}\).  Each is a rational polynomial obtained by summing at most \(R_{G,M}\) product-law monomials.  The ordered-profile-pair system in Definition \(\mathrm{def:mctfid\text{-}handle}\) is therefore a finite rational semialgebraic system.  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}decision}\) proves that the disjunction of these systems is satisfiable if and only if
\[
 \operatorname{GID}_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(Q)=0.
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}real\text{-}closed\text{-}field\text{-}decision}\) makes both the decision and, in the satisfiable case, exact algebraic sample-point extraction effective.

\paragraph{The empty-sign front end.}
Suppose \(M=\varnothing\).  Definition \(\mathrm{def:mctfid\text{-}handle}\) first runs conditional \(\mathsf{CTFID}\).  In this case Definition \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\) imposes no response-function restriction beyond the finite-binary recursive semi-Markovian conditions, so the model class in Definition \(\mathrm{def:identification\text{-}criterion}\) is the restriction to this theorem's domain of the unrestricted class appearing in Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}ctfid\text{-}completeness}\).  That lemma therefore gives
\[
 \mathsf{CTFID}(G,\mathcal Z,Q)\text{ succeeds}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{GID}_{G,\varnothing,\mathcal Z}(Q)=1
\]
on the stated finite-binary recursive semi-Markovian domain.  On success, the definition returns the CTFID expression unchanged, merely viewing it as an element of \(\mathcal R(p)\).  On CTFID failure, the displayed equivalence gives global nonidentification on this domain; Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}decision}\) then makes a canonical pair system satisfiable, so the continuation returns \((\mathsf{FAIL},\tau_{\mathsf F})\).  Thus, when \(M=\varnothing\), the MCTFID success set is exactly the CTFID success set on the common domain and the successful expression is its unchanged lift.

\paragraph{The M-ID front end and scoped containment.}
Suppose first that \(M\ne\varnothing\) and that \(\mathsf{MID}\) returns \(H\) on an input in the common domain.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:mid\text{-}soundness}\) gives
\[
 H(P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m))=\theta_Q(\mathfrak m)
\]
for every \(\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\) having \(P_{\mathfrak m}(B_Q)>0\).  Hence any two such models with the same menu law have equal query values, and Definition \(\mathrm{def:identification\text{-}criterion}\) gives \(\operatorname{GID}_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(Q)=1\).  Definition \(\mathrm{def:mctfid\text{-}handle}\) returns this same \(H\) before invoking the algebraic back end.

If instead \(M=\varnothing\) and \(\mathsf{MID}\) succeeds on an input in the common domain, the same soundness lemma implies identification in the finite-binary recursive semi-Markovian class.  Conditional CTFID completeness then makes the empty-sign front end succeed.  This proves, with both procedures restricted to the common domain,
\[
 \operatorname{Succ}(\mathsf{MID})
 \subseteq \operatorname{Succ}(\mathsf{MCTFID}).
\]
In the empty-sign case it does not identify the two returned expression trees, because the procedure actually runs CTFID there.

\paragraph{The failure branch.}
Suppose the finite pair disjunction is satisfiable.  Exact sample-point extraction supplies two enumerated signed-isotone profiles and two exact algebraic product-simplex mass vectors.  The profile constraints make every local table obey Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:signed\text{-}local\text{-}monotonicity}\), and the product-simplex constraints give mutually independent exogenous coordinates as required by Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:semi\text{-}markovian}\).  Thus the sampled objects are models \(\mathfrak m_0,\mathfrak m_1\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\), with \(|\Omega_u|\le b_u\).

For a district \(D\), all exogenous indices affecting its vertices lie in the block \(\{u:C(u)=D\}\).  These blocks are disjoint across districts, and their coordinates are independent.  The sampled models are therefore district-factorized.  The sampled equalities give, for every \(k\) and \(x\),
\[
 \phi_{a_0,k,x}(\lambda^0)
 =\phi_{a_1,k,x}(\lambda^1)
 =p^{\star}_{k,x},
\]
whereas the strict constraints give \(d_{a_0}(\lambda^0)>0\), \(d_{a_1}(\lambda^1)>0\), and
\[
 h_{a_0}(\lambda^0)d_{a_1}(\lambda^1)
 \ne
 h_{a_1}(\lambda^1)d_{a_0}(\lambda^0).
\]
Division is legitimate precisely because both displayed denominators are positive.  It follows that
\[
 P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m_0)=p^{\star}
 =P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m_1),
 \qquad
 \theta_Q(\mathfrak m_0)\ne\theta_Q(\mathfrak m_1).
\]
Definition \(\mathrm{def:fail\text{-}compiler\text{-}handle}\) deletes only zero-mass padding states and verifies exactly these constraints, so its decoded models retain all asserted properties.  Conversely, Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}decision}\) shows that failure of global identification on the stated class makes some enumerated pair system satisfiable.  Hence the algebraic back end returns a failure certificate exactly in the nonidentified case on that class.

\paragraph{Compilation of the identifying functional.}
It remains to treat an invocation of the algebraic back end for which the pair disjunction is unsatisfiable.  Consider the finite semialgebraic relation
\[
 \Gamma_Q
 =\bigcup_a\left\{(p,t):
 \exists\lambda\;\left[
 \Lambda_a(\lambda)\wedge p=\phi_a(\lambda)
 \wedge d_a(\lambda)>0
 \wedge t d_a(\lambda)=h_a(\lambda)
 \right]\right\}.
\]
It is effectively semialgebraic by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}real\text{-}closed\text{-}field\text{-}decision}\).  Every nonempty fiber over \(p\) is a singleton.  Indeed, two values \(t_0\ne t_1\) in one fiber would provide two feasible canonical models with the same menu cells and positive denominators.  Since \(t_i=h_{a_i}(\lambda^i)/d_{a_i}(\lambda^i)\), their inequality would be equivalent, after multiplication by the positive denominators, to the unequal cross-product in the pair system, contradicting its unsatisfiability.

Apply Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}cad\text{-}thom\text{-}sections}\) to rational polynomials defining \(\Gamma_Q\).  A finite sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition partitions the projected \(p\)-space into semialgebraic cells.  On every cell contained in the projection of \(\Gamma_Q\), its unique ordinate is a real-root section distinguished either by a rational isolating interval or by a finite Thom derivative-sign encoding.  Use the cell's rational polynomial sign description as a branch guard and the corresponding \(\operatorname{Root}_j\) or \(\operatorname{ThomRoot}_{\sigma}\) term as its value.  Assign the rational value zero to every cell outside the projection.  Definition \(\mathrm{def:expression\text{-}grammar}\) then gives a globally totalized finite expression \(F\in\mathcal R(p)\).

This construction is effective in the precise input model of that definition.  At an arbitrary real \(p\), exact polynomial-sign queries select the active branch and the certified root section supplies its exact value.  If \(p\) has rational or real-algebraic coordinates, sign determination, algebraic arithmetic, Thom encodings, and real-root isolation give a finite exact evaluation algorithm.  No step requires a finite bit representation of an arbitrary transcendental input.

Now let \(\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\) satisfy \(P_{\mathfrak m}(B_Q)>0\).  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:signed\text{-}canonical\text{-}reduction}\) supplies a canonical model preserving its menu law, query numerator, and query denominator.  Thus
\[
 \bigl(P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m),\theta_Q(\mathfrak m)\bigr)
 \in\Gamma_Q.
\]
The singleton-fiber construction consequently gives
\[
 F(P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m))=\theta_Q(\mathfrak m).
\]
This also separates the causal target \(\theta_Q(\mathfrak m)\) from the observed-law functional \(F\): their equality is a theorem on the positive-denominator model class, not a definition.

If either front end returns an expression, its declared soundness gives global identification on the common domain.  If the algebraic back end returns an expression, unsatisfiability of the pair system and Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}decision}\) give global identification there.  Conversely, if the criterion equals one, the pair system is unsatisfiable; unless a sound front end has already returned, the preceding CAD construction returns \(F\).  Therefore, with the domain restriction understood on both sides,
\[
 \operatorname{Succ}(\mathsf{MCTFID})
 =\{(G,M,\mathcal Z,Q):\operatorname{GID}_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(Q)=1\}.
\]
Together with the scoped containment already proved, this is the claimed success-set identity.

Finally, all response-table sets, profile sets, polynomial systems, and CAD cell decompositions are finite.  At most \(A_{G,M}\) profiles and \(A_{G,M}^2\) ordered pairs are examined, with the coordinate and latent-configuration bounds proved above.  Termination of every exact decision, sample-point, and root-section compilation call follows from the two declared effective real-algebraic lemmas.  The argument establishes completeness only for the class fixed in the first paragraph; it neither extends that completeness to the broader ordered-variable or general-SCM domain of the published M-ID work nor supplies a district-local graphical failure compiler.  This proves the theorem exactly at its stated scope.

statements.statement:
With both success sets restricted to the common finite-binary recursive semi-Markovian signed-local-monotonicity domain of Definition \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\), the inclusion
\[
 \operatorname{Succ}(\mathsf{MID})
 \subseteq
 \operatorname{Succ}(\mathsf{MCTFID})
\]
is strict.  A witness is the three-vertex DAG \(G\) with directed edges \(X\to Y\leftarrow Z\), no bidirected edges, positive signs on both directed edges, the observational menu \(\mathcal Z=\{\varnothing\}\), and the positive-denominator query
\[
 Q=P\bigl(Y_{11}=1\mid Y_{10}=1,\,Y_{01}=1\bigr),
\]
where the two subscript coordinates give the interventions on \((X,Z)\).  For this witness \(\operatorname{GID}_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(Q)=1\), so \(\mathsf{MCTFID}\) returns an identifying expression \(F\) satisfying
\[
 F(P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m))=1
\]
for every compatible model \(\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\) with \(P_{\mathfrak m}(B_Q)>0\), whereas the published \(\mathsf{MID}\) procedure returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\).  Hence the published \(\mathsf{MID}\) procedure is not success-set maximal even on the common three-binary-variable unconfounded DAG subclass.  This conclusion does not claim that \(\mathsf{MCTFID}\) solves the broader ordered-variable or general-SCM completeness problem considered by the published \(\mathsf{MID}\) work.
statements.proof_tex:
\paragraph{Construction and support conditions.}
Let the endogenous variables \(X,Z,Y\) be binary.  Take \(G\) to have precisely the directed edges \(X\to Y\) and \(Z\to Y\), with no bidirected edges, and put
\[
 M=\{((X,Y),+1),((Z,Y),+1)\}.
\]
The graph is finite and acyclic, and with the private exogenous variables of the recursive semi-Markovian expansion it belongs to the common domain stated in the theorem.  The menu consists only of the full observational population law, so \(K=1\) and \(\mathcal Z=\{\varnothing\}\).  Write \(Y_{xz}\) for the response of \(Y\) under \(\operatorname{do}(X=x,Z=z)\), and define
\[
 A_Q=\{Y_{11}=1\},
 \qquad
 B_Q=\{Y_{10}=1,Y_{01}=1\}.
\]
The query is considered only at models satisfying \(P_{\mathfrak m}(B_Q)>0\).  No observational-cell positivity or overlap condition is used.

The positive-denominator domain is nonempty.  Indeed, take mutually independent binary exogenous variables for the three vertices, let \(X=U_X\), \(Z=U_Z\), and let
\[
 Y=X\lor Z.
\]
This is a recursive semi-Markovian model over \(G\), its \(Y\)-mechanism is nondecreasing in each signed parent, and \(Y_{10}=Y_{01}=1\) for every exogenous assignment.  Hence \(P(B_Q)=1\).

\paragraph{Identification in the signed-monotone class.}
Fix an arbitrary \(\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\).  By Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:signed\text{-}local\text{-}monotonicity}\), for every exogenous assignment \(u\), monotonicity of the edge \(Z\to Y\), with \(X=1\) fixed, gives
\[
 Y_{10}(u)\le Y_{11}(u).
\]
Equally, monotonicity of \(X\to Y\), with \(Z=1\) fixed, gives
\[
 Y_{01}(u)\le Y_{11}(u).
\]
Because all responses are binary, either inequality shows that
\[
 \{Y_{10}=1,Y_{01}=1\}\subseteq\{Y_{11}=1\}.
\]
Consequently \(A_Q\cap B_Q=B_Q\).  On the stipulated positive-denominator domain, division is legitimate and
\[
 \theta_Q(\mathfrak m)
 =\frac{P_{\mathfrak m}(A_Q\cap B_Q)}{P_{\mathfrak m}(B_Q)}
 =\frac{P_{\mathfrak m}(B_Q)}{P_{\mathfrak m}(B_Q)}
 =1.
\]
Thus any two models in \(\mathfrak M(G,M)\) with positive query denominators have equal query values, whether or not their menu laws agree.  Definition \(\mathrm{def:identification\text{-}criterion}\) yields
\[
 \operatorname{GID}_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(Q)=1.
\]
Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}oracle\text{-}complete\text{-}mctfid}\), at its expressly finite-binary recursive semi-Markovian scope, now implies that \(\mathsf{MCTFID}(G,M,\mathcal Z,Q)\) succeeds and returns some \(F\in\mathcal R(p)\) satisfying
\[
 F(P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m))=\theta_Q(\mathfrak m)=1
\]
for every compatible model \(\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\) with \(P_{\mathfrak m}(B_Q)>0\).  This distinguishes the causal target from the identifying map: the causal equality \(\theta_Q(\mathfrak m)=1\) was derived pointwise from the structural order restriction, and equality with \(F\) follows only afterward from scoped oracle completeness.  Nothing in this argument constrains the arbitrary totalization of \(F\) outside the compatible positive-denominator projection.

\paragraph{Exact failure trace for \(\mathsf{MID}\).}
Run the published \(\mathsf{MID}\) algorithm on this same input.  Ordinary conditional ancestral reduction cannot discard either conditioning literal: \(Y_{11}\), \(Y_{10}\), and \(Y_{01}\) are responses of the same primitive vertex and belong to the ancestral component containing the queried response.  Since each subscript already fixes the complete parent set \((X,Z)\), the single relevant ctf-factor passed to the monotonicity-reduction subroutine is
\[
 P(Y_{11}=1,Y_{10}=1,Y_{01}=1).
\]
In the Boolean order on the two positive monotone-parent coordinates,
\[
 (1,0)\le(1,1),
 \qquad
 (0,1)\le(1,1).
\]
The simplification rule for two equal one-valued responses at ordered assignments therefore deletes the redundant upper literal \(Y_{11}=1\).  After all such simplifications, the factor is
\[
 P(Y_{10}=1,Y_{01}=1).
\]
Neither remaining literal is redundant, because
\[
 (1,0)\not\le(0,1)
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 (0,1)\not\le(1,0).
\]
Hence the two parent assignments are not totally ordered.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:mid\text{-}incomparable\text{-}failure}\) shows first that the reduction subroutine returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\) and then that \(\mathsf{MID}\) propagates this output.  In particular, this failure occurs before the algorithm forms its final numerator-to-denominator ratio, so it does not cancel the common factor.  Therefore
\[
 \mathsf{MID}(G,M,\mathcal Z,Q)=\mathsf{FAIL},
 \qquad
 \mathsf{MCTFID}(G,M,\mathcal Z,Q)\ne\mathsf{FAIL}.
\]

The weak inclusion on the common domain is part of Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}oracle\text{-}complete\text{-}mctfid}\).  The displayed witness lies in the right-hand success set and outside the left-hand success set, proving strictness on that domain.  Since the witness itself is an unconfounded three-binary-variable DAG, it also proves that the published M-ID procedure is not success-set maximal even on that common subclass.  This witness supplies no implication about oracle completeness outside the finite-binary recursive semi-Markovian class.

\paragraph{Finite response-type sanity check and load-bearing restriction.}
Order the four values of a deterministic isotone response table as \((Y_{00},Y_{01},Y_{10},Y_{11})\).  The six possible tables are
\[
 0000,\quad 0001,\quad 0011,\quad 0101,\quad 0111,\quad 1111.
\]
The event \(B_Q\) selects exactly the last two tables \(0111\) and \(1111\), and both have \(Y_{11}=1\), confirming the pointwise argument by exhaustive enumeration.  If the two positive monotonicity restrictions are removed, the binary table \(0110\), realized for example by \(Y=X\mathbin{\oplus}Z\), has \(B_Q=1\) but \(A_Q=0\).  Thus signed local monotonicity is load-bearing for the identifying value one.
statements.justification: The exact three-vertex witness proves that the published M-ID procedure is not success-set maximal even on the common unconfounded three-binary-variable DAG subclass.
statements.gap: MaitiPleckoBareinboim2025 gives sound monotonicity reductions but its reduction fails when one ctf-factor retains incomparable monotone-parent assignments; the witness is nevertheless identified pointwise by isotonicity and by the scoped complete oracle.
statements.consumer: Maiti's M-ID implementation can use this witness as a regression test for future reductions, while fairness analyses with the same response pattern can use the constant identifying functional.

statements.statement: Every first-order formula over a real closed field whose atomic predicates are polynomial equalities or inequalities can be eliminated effectively to an equivalent quantifier-free formula.  In particular, closed formulas are decidable, and a satisfiable finite semialgebraic system with rational coefficients admits exact algebraic sample-point extraction.

The Block Elimination Algorithm also produces a set of parametrized sample points which are guaranteed to meet each semi-algebraically connected component of the set of realizable sign conditions.

Let \(Y_1,Y_2,\ldots\) be independent and identically distributed random vectors in \(\mathbb R^d\) with mean \(\mu\), finite second moment, and covariance matrix \(\Sigma\). If \(\overline Y_m=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^mY_i\), then
\[
 \sqrt m\,\bigl(\overline Y_m-\mu\bigr)\rightsquigarrow N_d(0,\Sigma).
\]

source.verbatim_statement: 2.18 Example (Multivariate central limit theorem). Let Y₁, Y₂, ... be i.i.d. random vectors in ℝᵏ with mean vector μ = EY₁ and covariance matrix Σ = E(Y₁ − μ)(Y₁ − μ)ᵀ. Then (1/√n)∑ᵢ₌₁ⁿ(Yᵢ − μ) = √n(Ȳₙ − μ) ⇝ Nₖ(0, Σ).

Let \(a_n\to\infty\), let \(T_n\) be random vectors taking values in a subset of \(\mathbb R^d\), and suppose that \(a_n(T_n-\vartheta)\rightsquigarrow T\). If \(\phi\) is defined on a neighborhood of \(\vartheta\) and is differentiable at \(\vartheta\), then
\[
 a_n\{\phi(T_n)-\phi(\vartheta)\}\rightsquigarrow \phi'_{\vartheta}(T).
\]

source.verbatim_statement: 3.1 Theorem. Let φ : Dφ ⊂ ℝᵏ → ℝᵐ be a map defined on a subset of ℝᵏ and differentiable at θ. Let Tₙ be random vectors taking their values in the domain of φ. If rₙ(Tₙ − θ) ⇝ T for numbers rₙ → ∞, then rₙ(φ(Tₙ) − φ(θ)) ⇝ φ′θ(T). Moreover, the difference between rₙ(φ(Tₙ) − φ(θ)) and φ′θ(rₙ(Tₙ − θ)) converges to zero in probability.

statements.statement: Given finitely many rational polynomials, an effective sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition partitions real space into finitely many semialgebraic cells with exact sample points.  Over each base cell, its sections are graphs of continuous semialgebraic real-root functions, and a real root is uniquely distinguished by its Thom derivative-sign encoding.

Given a Thom encoding σ, x(σ) denotes the root specified by σ. Points are represented by univariate representations and an associated Thom encoding.

sampling_model.design: \(K\) independent regime-specific multinomial samples from the known observational or interventional menu \(\mathcal Z\).
sampling_model.units: Regime \(k\) contains \(n_k\) independent units with cell law \(p_k\), and \(n_k/n\to\rho_k\in(0,1)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Each regime fixes its declared intervention \(z_k\); the empty intervention is observational sampling.
sampling_model.overlap: The query denominator is bounded below by \(\kappa>0\) on the sampling-law fiber, and the local analytic margin \(\lambda_F(p)\) bounds branch guards, active denominators, root derivatives, and isolating-interval separation away from zero.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nonparametric nuisance is introduced; every input is a finite empirical cell vector, and differentiation is recursive on the locally fixed analytic branch of the returned expression tree.

estimand_functional: \(\theta_Q(\mathfrak m)=F(P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m))\) when \(\mathsf{MCTFID}(G,M,\mathcal Z,Q)=F\), with \(\widehat\theta_Q=F(\widehat p)\)

tldr: For finite binary semi-Markovian diagrams, local signed monotonicity deletes most Boolean response functions but invalidates the parity countermodels used in unrestricted completeness proofs. The project first proves a signed canonical finite-SCM reduction with an explicit Dedekind-number support bound and a global semialgebraic identification oracle. Its open kernel is to compress that oracle into a terminating district-compositional \(\mathsf{MCTFID}\) calculus built from an order-annotated AMWN and canonical order-normal cells, with one menu-law functional exactly for globally identified queries and a failed trace compiled into two legal signed-isotone SCMs together with their common observable law. The calculus must reduce to ordinary CTFID when \(M=\varnothing\), reproduce every M-ID success, expose whether that inclusion is strict, and feed a locally branch-stable finite-cell central limit theorem and Wald interval.

project_justification.gap: MaitiPleckoBareinboim2025 proves sound monotonicity reductions but explicitly leaves a sufficient-and-necessary general algorithm open. Unrestricted completeness proofs in CorreaLeeBareinboim2021 and RaghavanBareinboim2026 use countermodels whose parity mechanisms violate signed local monotonicity, while canonical finite-SCM programs do not yield a district-compositional identifying calculus.
project_justification.niche: The finite binary setting admits exact order geometry: after sign normalization, each local response table is an up-set of a Boolean lattice and has a Dedekind-number count. This creates a finite oracle and a concrete target for replacing parity with composable threshold atoms without narrowing the published signed-monotone model class.
project_justification.fill: The project builds a canonical order-normal AMWN representation, proves its district factorization, derives a terminating complete symbolic procedure with explicit state and response-type bounds, and requires every failure to carry two finite order-respecting SCMs and their common menu law. A multisample delta method on a certified locally fixed analytic branch then turns every fixed successful expression into an empirical-cell estimator and confidence interval.

related_work: MaitiPleckoBareinboim2025 supplies the writing arc and the local monotonicity reduction and difference rules, but its conclusion identifies full necessity and sufficiency as the missing endpoint. CorreaLeeBareinboim2021 supplies counterfactual unnesting, ancestral reduction, district factorization, and complete CTFID for arbitrary observational and interventional menus. CorreaBareinboim2025 supplies the AMWN construction and ctf-calculus transformations that the order annotations refine. RaghavanBareinboim2026 supplies the closest failure-to-countermodel compiler, but its mod-two parent sums and flipped parity bit are not isotone. ZhangTianBareinboim2022 supplies the canonical finite-SCM equivalence proof; restricting its canonical partitions to signed-isotone response functions yields the proposed Dedekind count. LeeCorreaBareinboim2020 and ShpitserPearl2008 explain how hedgelets, thickets, and district recursion certify unrestricted necessity. DuarteEtAl2024 supplies a general polynomial-program oracle against which the graphical calculus can be regression-tested. BhattacharyaNabiShpitser2022 supplies the identification-to-estimation compiler pattern, while PleckoBareinboim2024 supplies the direct, indirect, spurious, and variable-specific counterfactual consumer family. HashimotoKawakamiTian2026 studies monotonicity bounds for a single-treatment ordinal potential-outcome setting and does not occupy the arbitrary-diagram, arbitrary-menu signed calculus target.
technical_internal_limitation: A finite canonical parameterization makes global identification decidable by real algebraic methods, so mere decidability is not the novelty claim. The load-bearing claim is district-compositional compression with a checkable signed countermodel trace. Restricting successful outputs to rational expressions could be false because finite polynomial model classes can identify algebraic but non-rational functions; the grammar therefore includes uniquely isolated real roots and requires ordinary CTFID outputs as the rational special case. Inference is asserted only where every branch guard and active algebraic operation is separated from its singular boundary by \(\lambda_F(p)\ge\kappa\).
honest_scope: The signed canonical reduction, global finite decision theorem, order-normal factorization, explicit empty-sign reduction, and locally branch-stable plug-in limit are theorem targets with direct finite constructions. The genuinely open content is the composable threshold countermodel compiler and the equivalence between its terminal obstructions and every globally nonidentified graph-menu-query instance. The sanity reduction recomputes \(D_0=2\) and \(T_v=2^{2^{|\operatorname{pa}_G(v)|}}\) when \(M=\varnothing\), after which the procedure must agree extensionally with ordinary CTFID; every M-ID success must also be reproduced. The scope excludes nested syntax before unnesting, continuous endogenous variables, zero conditioning denominators, inference at branch boundaries, and data-dependent selection among empirically tied formulas.
